article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Evening Brief
article.dek: The inactives are out for tonight's Bills-Vikings game — Buffalo is missing both starters on the left side of its line — and the Monday total has climbed two points since this morning.

items.headline: Lead: Buffalo loses the whole left side of its line, 90 minutes before kickoff
paragraphs: The inactive lists are out for tonight's Bills-Vikings game, and the big news is on Buffalo's side. Left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson are both out. That is the entire left side of the offensive line that protects Josh Allen's blind side.

Tylan Grable is expected to start at left tackle and Austin Corbett at left guard. They walk into a loud dome against Brian Flores' Vikings defense, the heaviest-blitzing defense in the league. That is a tough first test for two backups.

Minnesota's side is settled. Kyler Murray is out with his hamstring injury, so Carson Wentz starts at quarterback, with Max Brosmer as the backup. Receiver Jauan Jennings is out too, and safety Theo Jackson is out. Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis.
items.takeaway: Dawkins and Anderson are both out — Buffalo's left side is two backups tonight against the league's heaviest-blitzing defense. Wentz starts for Minnesota.

items.headline: Injuries: Ferguson and Goodson out for weeks, Locke ruled out, Pickens still a question
paragraphs: The Cowboys imaging the morning brief was waiting on came back, and it is bad news. Tight end Jake Ferguson sprained two ligaments in his left knee — the PCL and the MCL — and will miss multiple weeks. Running back Tyler Goodson is out multiple weeks with a knee injury too.
Safety P.J. Locke has been ruled out against the 49ers on November 15. It is his second concussion in as many weeks, and the team says he will likely miss multiple games.
Receiver George Pickens is in the rehab group this week. Whether he plays against the 49ers gets decided during the week. Tight end Luke Schoonmaker is expected back to help at the position.
items.takeaway: Ferguson (sprained PCL and MCL) and Goodson are out multiple weeks; Locke is ruled out against the 49ers; Pickens is still a week-to-week call.

items.headline: Weather: tonight is indoors, so weather is a non-factor
paragraphs: Bills-Vikings is at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, which has a roof. No wind, no rain, no cold to adjust for. Weather does not change anything about tonight's game. There is no NFL game tomorrow, so there is nothing to forecast for Tuesday either.
items.takeaway: Tonight is indoors in Minneapolis — weather is a non-factor, and there is no game tomorrow.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — last week's cards are still showing, so tonight goes through Check
paragraphs: The app board still shows Week 8. It was generated November 2 and has not flipped to Week 9, let alone Week 10 — I checked again at 6:10 p.m. Denver time and it is the same board as this morning. The headline cards on it are from last Monday night's Bears-Seahawks game: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win — the Seahawks moneyline, with the model at 56.1% against a market price that needed 60.4%. It forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the model's plus-EV play — the Bears +3, with the model at 50.6% against a market that needed 50.5%, for a small positive edge.

One more thing the board has not picked up: it still shows Kyler Murray as Minnesota's expected starter, from a stale Week 8 snapshot. Carson Wentz is the one starting tonight — that comes from the team, not the app. For tonight, there is no card to read, so use Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price for Bills-Vikings, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override. Monday game? Monday check.
items.takeaway: The board still shows last week's Week 8 cards and still lists Murray as Minnesota's starter, so tonight's Bills-Vikings price goes through Check — type in your book's line and price and let the app give you a verdict on it.

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers — why -3 and -3.5 are not the same bet
paragraphs: A key number is a final margin that shows up a lot. In the NFL, 3 is the big one — more games end with a team winning by exactly 3 than by any other margin, because a field goal is the most common scoring play. That makes -3 and -3.5 very different bets.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you take a favorite at -3 at -110. If they win by exactly 3, you push — your stake comes back, no win, no loss. Take the same favorite at -3.5 instead, and a win by exactly 3 loses your bet. Same team, same game, same result — but the half point turns a push into a loss.

That is why tonight's move matters as a lesson, not a pick. The Bills went from -3 this morning to -3.5 at most books. If your book still shows -3, that half point is worth something — run it through Check and let the app judge your price. And if your book shows -3.5, know what you are paying for: you need a win by 4 or more.
items.takeaway: Three is the most common winning margin in the NFL, so -3 can push where -3.5 loses — the half point matters, and a book still showing -3 is a better price than one showing -3.5.

items.headline: The spread crossed 3 and the total bounced back two points since this morning
paragraphs: The Bills were -3 this morning at DraftKings and FanDuel. They are -3.5 at most books now, with the Vikings +3.5 at -115 at DraftKings. The spread moved a half point toward Buffalo and crossed the key number 3.

The total moved the other way from where the week was headed. It fell four points during the week, from 47.5 down to 43.5 this morning. Since this morning it has climbed back to 45.5 at most books. The morning's 43.5 is gone.

The app board has caught none of this. It still shows Week 8 prices from November 2, and there is no Bills-Vikings game on it at all. If your book's number for tonight looks different from the ones above, run it through Check and let the app judge your price, not last week's.
items.takeaway: Bills -3 to -3.5, total 43.5 to 45.5 since this morning — the morning's numbers are gone at most books.

items.headline: One game left — if Check says bet on your number, bet it now
paragraphs: There is one price left this week, and kickoff is about two hours away. If you like a side or a total tonight, run your book's exact price through Check. If it says bet, bet the good number now — the total already moved two points today, and the spread crossed 3. Waiting for kickoff risks a worse price, not a better one.
Wait only if your bet depends on a name that is still undecided — and tonight's inactives are already out, so there is nothing left to wait for. Monday game? Monday check.
items.takeaway: Run tonight's price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now; the inactives are out and the numbers have already moved twice today.

evidence.fact: Bills at Vikings inactives, Monday Nov 9 (released about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff): Buffalo is without starting left tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs) and starting left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) — the entire left side of the offensive line. Tylan Grable is expected to start at left tackle and Austin Corbett at left guard. Also inactive for Buffalo: WR Skyler Bell, S Jalon Kilgore, OLB Mike Danna, DL Greg Gaines. WR Joshua Palmer was placed on injured reserve Monday (hamstring). For Minnesota: QB Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out and Carson Wentz starts, backed up by Max Brosmer; WR Jauan Jennings (calf) is out; S Theo Jackson (quad) is out; also inactive: S Jakobe Thomas, CB Chuck Demmings, DL Caleb Banks (healthy scratch). RB Demond Claiborne was placed on injured reserve (knee); WR Odell Beckham Jr. was signed to the active roster.
evidence.interpretation: Buffalo's line is the night's biggest change since the morning brief: the left side that protects Josh Allen's blind side is two backups against the heaviest-blitzing defense in the league. Minnesota's QB picture is unchanged — Wentz starts.
evidence.app_guidance: If you bet tonight, this is the news that matters most — check whether your book's number moved on it, then run your price through Check.

evidence.fact: Cowboys injury news, Monday Nov 9: TE Jake Ferguson will miss multiple weeks with sprained posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligaments in his left knee, suffered in the third quarter Sunday against the Colts. RB Tyler Goodson will also miss multiple weeks with a knee injury. S P.J. Locke has been ruled out against the 49ers on Nov 15 after his second concussion in as many weeks and will likely miss multiple games. WR George Pickens (hamstring) is in the rehab group this week, with his status for Nov 15 to be determined during the week. TE Luke Schoonmaker is expected to return from injury to help the tight end depth chart.
evidence.interpretation: The imaging the morning brief was waiting on came back bad: Ferguson and Goodson are multi-week absences, and Locke is out too. Dallas goes into the 49ers game short at tight end, running back depth, and safety.
evidence.app_guidance: This is next week's news, not tonight's — it matters when the board flips to Week 10 and Dallas prices appear.

evidence.fact: Bills at Vikings, Monday Nov 9 evening: the spread is now Bills -3.5 at most books (DraftKings, FanDuel, Circa, Pinnacle, BookMaker were -3 this morning), with Vikings +3.5 at -115 at DraftKings and Bills -3.5 at +100 at BetMGM. The total has climbed back to 45.5 at most books (DraftKings, BetMGM, Novig) after sitting at 43.5 at DraftKings and FanDuel this morning. Opening line was Bills -2.5 with a total of 47.5. Moneyline: Bills about -180 to -198, Vikings about +150 to +165.
evidence.interpretation: Two moves since the morning brief: the spread crossed the key number 3 to -3.5 toward Buffalo, and the total bounced two points back up after falling four points during the week. The market is pricing a slower game, and the morning's 43.5 total is gone.
evidence.app_guidance: If your book still shows -3 or 43.5, that number is better than the market now — run it through Check before it moves.

evidence.fact: Bills at Vikings, Monday Nov 9, 8:15 p.m. ET, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, which has a roof. The game is indoors. There are no NFL games on Tuesday Nov 10.
evidence.interpretation: Weather is a non-factor tonight, and there is no game tomorrow to forecast for.
evidence.app_guidance: No weather adjustment needed for tonight's game.

evidence.fact: NFL EDGE product endpoint checked Monday Nov 9, about 6:10 p.m. Denver time, and re-fetched at 6:11 p.m.: the board still shows Week 8, generated 2026-11-02T12:08:54Z — the same board as this morning, byte-identical. Headline cards are all from Bears at Seahawks (2026_08_CHI_SEA): Hit Rate Seahawks moneyline -175, model probability 56.1% vs market 60.4%, EV -0.0568; Balanced and Value both Bears +3 at -102, model probability 50.6% vs market 46.5%, EV +0.0356. Thirteen of fourteen Week 8 games show IN_PROGRESS with empty market boards. There is no Week 9 game on the board at all — no Bills-Vikings game, and the app's quarterback fields still show Kyler Murray as Minnesota's expected starter from the stale Week 8 snapshot, not Carson Wentz.
evidence.interpretation: The evening refresh did not flip the board. Its cards are last week's games and must not be bet, and it has not picked up tonight's quarterback change either.
evidence.app_guidance: Tonight's prices go through Check until the board flips; do not trust the app's quarterback fields for tonight.
